summary.headline: Only 3.6% of Chinese model releases published safety tests
summary.body: A SemiAnalysis study reported by the FT found Chinese developers published safety evaluations for just 3.6% of 857 model releases, arguing Beijing will not 'pace the frontier'. That weakens both Alignment & Control and Global Coordination, lifting Conquerors and Zookeeper. Capability kept rising too: Meta released Muse Wonder, its first frontier-class model, and BloombergNEF projected China will spend $3.9T through 2049 moving power to AI data centres. Police use of Graylark's Raven, which can locate a home from one interior photo, added to Surveillance & Control. Horizon Balance fell to -13.69.
summary.movers_note: Conquerors +0.3 (safety-test study +0.17, Muse Wonder +0.09, China grid +0.06), Zookeeper +0.3 (+0.12, +0.09 and +0.06) and Reversion -0.2 (Muse Wonder -0.11, China grid -0.08).

events.title: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier-class model
events.summary: Meta launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full for agentic tasks, priced near Claude Opus 5.5 but trailing it on benchmarks.
events.reason: New frontier entrant from a major lab.

events.title: China projected to spend $3.9T on grid to power AI data centers
events.summary: BloombergNEF projects China will spend $3.9T through 2049 moving inland wind and solar power to coastal AI data centers; State Grid plans ~$574B over five years.
events.reason: Long-horizon national compute-energy buildout; projection rather than event.

events.title: AI tool lets police pinpoint a home from a single interior photo
events.summary: Graylark's Raven (formerly GeoSpy) lets police upload one interior photo and identify the specific house or rental by matching public Airbnb, Zillow and Vrbo listings; LAPD and Miami-Dade are users.
events.reason: New AI police surveillance capability in use by large departments.
